locators: p. 15, Box 5. Interest Income, "Report interest income on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b"

findings.who: A partner whose Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) prints "STMT", "See Statement" or an asterisk in box 6a. The dividend figure appears only on the attached supplemental statement, which partnerships often use when they report several activities or break out dividends.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 6a "show[s] an amount". The box itself shows a word or symbol, not a number, so a literal reader answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6a: "Report ordinary dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b." The same page also says: "The partnership attached a statement to the Schedule K-1 identifying the dividends included in box 6a or 6b"
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 6a (ordinary dividends) show an amount, or refer you to an attached statement (for example 'STMT' or '*') that gives one?" Help: "If the box points to a statement, answer yes and enter the total ordinary dividends from the statement."

findings.who: Same partner as above. The qualified-dividend figure is also given on the statement rather than in box 6b.
findings.why_no: The 6b line is reached only through the box 6a gate. A no caused by "STMT" in box 6a also drops the qualified dividends.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6b: "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a."
findings.fix: Same broadened gate as above. Add to the 6b question: "include qualified dividends shown on an attached statement."

findings.who: A partner whose K-1, through a partnership error, leaves box 6a blank but shows an amount in box 6b.
findings.why_no: Box 6a truthfully shows no amount, so the gate is no. The 6b amount is never asked, and nothing prompts the filer to get a corrected K-1.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6b: "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 6a or 6b show an amount?" If 6b exceeds 6a, flag the inconsistency (the help already says 6b is never more than 6a).

locators: p. 15, Box 6a. Ordinary Dividends, "Report ordinary dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b"
p. 15, Box 6b. Qualified Dividends, "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a"

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 shows "STMT", "See attached" or an asterisk in box 8 instead of a number. The partnership reports the net short-term capital gain or loss on a supplemental statement, which is common for tiered or multi-activity partnerships.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 8 "show[s] an amount". The box itself shows no figure, only a reference to a statement, so the filer reads it literally and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8: "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 8 (net short-term capital gain or loss) show an amount, or refer to an attached statement that reports one? Answer yes for a gain or a loss, including an amount in parentheses."

findings.who: A partner whose box 8 shows a loss printed in parentheses, such as (2,350), with no minus sign.
findings.why_no: The filer may read the parenthesized figure as not "an amount" or not a "gain", and answer no. The partnership's short-term loss is then dropped from Schedule D, line 5.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8. Net Short-Term Capital Gain (Loss): "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Add help text: "A loss is often printed in parentheses; it is still an amount. Answer yes."

findings.who: Any partner who answers yes to the gate.
findings.why_no: No wrong no results. The gated line repeats the gate as a helper choice ("Box 8 shows an amount" true → line 8, false → zero). If the helper and the gate diverged, a yes could still yield zero.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8: "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Bind the line's choice directly to the gate input k1p.has_b8, or drop the redundant helper and use k1p.box8 whenever the gate is yes.

locators: p. 15, Box 8. Net Short-Term Capital Gain (Loss), "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership had collectibles gain (for example, $500 from sold art or coins) offset by an equal other net long-term capital loss. Box 9a nets to zero and is left blank, but box 9b shows $500. The filer also has $10,000 of long-term gains from stock sales elsewhere on the return.
findings.why_no: Box 9a, net long-term capital gain (loss), shows no amount, so the filer truthfully answers no. The 9b/9c question is never reached.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (forced false), so the box 9b collectibles amount never reaches line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet and $500 is taxed at 15% instead of 28%
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 in the Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040)."
findings.fix: Do not nest the 9b/9c question under box 9a. Ask it on every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065): "Does box 9b (collectibles 28% gain or loss) or box 9c (unrecaptured section 1250 gain) show an amount or refer to an attached statement, even if box 9a is blank or zero?"

findings.who: A partner in a real estate partnership that sold depreciated buildings at a gain and investment property at a loss. The net long-term result is zero, so box 9a is blank, but box 9c shows unrecaptured section 1250 gain. The filer has other long-term gains on the return.
findings.why_no: Box 9a shows no amount. The help text "Both are parts of the gain in box 9a" reinforces the belief that 9b and 9c cannot matter without 9a.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (forced false), so the 25% unrecaptured section 1250 gain is omitted from the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16, Box 9c: "Report unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale or exchange of the partnership's business assets on line 5."
findings.fix: Gate the 9b/9c question independently of 9a. Revise the help to: "These are usually parts of box 9a, but they can show amounts even when box 9a is blank or zero."

findings.who: A partner whose box 9a shows "STMT" or "See attached" instead of a figure, with the net long-term capital gain or loss given on a partnership statement. This is common for multi-activity or tiered partnerships.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 9a "show[s] an amount", and the box itself contains no dollar figure.
findings.line: k1p.box9a_if_any (zero instead of the net long-term capital gain or loss for Schedule D line 12)
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 9a: "Report the net long-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 12."
findings.fix: "Does box 9a show an amount, or a code or note such as STMT referring to an attached statement that gives a net long-term capital gain or loss?" with help: "If the amount is on a statement, answer yes and enter the statement's figure."

findings.who: A partner in a fund-of-funds partnership that passes through unrecaptured section 1250 gain from a REIT or RIC. Per the instructions, the partnership reports this on an attached statement rather than as a dollar amount in box 9c.
findings.why_no: Asked whether box 9c "show[s] an amount", the filer sees only a statement reference in the box and answers no.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (false), so the REIT/RIC unrecaptured section 1250 gain for worksheet line 11 is omitted
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16: "If it reports the other two types of unrecaptured gain, it'll provide an attached statement that shows the amount for each type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain."
findings.fix: "Does box 9b or 9c show an amount, or does the partnership attach a statement reporting collectibles gain or any type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain?"

locators: p. 15, Box 9a. Net Long-Term Capital Gain (Loss), "Report the net long-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 12"
p. 16, Box 9b. Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss), "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership had collectibles gain or unrecaptured section 1250 gain that was fully offset by other long-term capital losses. For example, $10,000 of collectibles gain and a $10,000 long-term loss leave box 9a at 0 or blank, while box 9b shows $10,000 or box 9c shows unrecaptured gain.
findings.why_no: The parent gate asks only whether box 9a shows an amount. When the partnership's netting leaves box 9a at zero or blank, the gate is false, and the box 9b and 9c question is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"; Box 9c: "Report your share of this unrecaptured gain on the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet". Neither instruction is conditioned on box 9a.
findings.fix: Remove the box 9a dependency. Ask on every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065): "Does box 9b or box 9c show an amount or 'STMT' (even if box 9a is blank or zero)?"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership reports more than one type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain, for example from a REIT, a RIC or a lower-tier partnership interest. Box 9c then reads 'STMT' and the amounts are on an attached statement.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 9b or 9c 'shows an amount'. 'STMT' is not a dollar amount, so the partner answers no. The help that says the STMT case is outside the tool's scope is attached only to the gated question, so it never appears and the tool never refuses.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9c: "If it reports the other two types of unrecaptured gain, it'll provide an attached statement that shows the amount for each type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain."
findings.fix: Word the gate as "Does box 9b or 9c show an amount, a loss, or 'STMT'?" Move the STMT-is-out-of-scope help onto the gate question itself.

findings.who: A partner whose box 9a shows a net long-term capital loss in parentheses, for example (15,000), while box 9b shows a $5,000 collectibles gain.
findings.why_no: If the box 9a condition is answered by the filer and not computed from an entered amount, the label 'net long-term capital gain (loss)' and 'shows an amount' may lead the filer to say no when the box holds a loss.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"
findings.fix: Compute the condition from the entered box 9a amount (nonzero, including negative values). If it is asked, say "any amount, including a loss shown in parentheses." This is better resolved by the first fix, which removes the dependency.

locators: p. 16, Box 9b. Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss), "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"
p. 16, Box 9c. Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain, "If the partnership reports only unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale or exchange of its business assets, it’ll enter a dollar amount in box 9c"

findings.who: A partner has a prior-year unallowed passive loss from this partnership on Form 8582, Part VII, column (c). Their 2025 Schedule K-1 shows nothing in boxes 1, 2 or 3. For example, the activity broke even, the K-1 reports only box 4 or other items, or the final K-1 for an interest sold in 2025 shows no ordinary or rental amount.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed false whenever boxes 1–3 are blank. The filer is never asked about a held-back loss, so the carryover is set to zero.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582." The column takes the carryover whether or not the activity has current-year income or loss in columns (a)/(b).
findings.fix: Do not condition the held-back-loss question on boxes 1–3. Ask it for every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065): 'Did your 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII, column (c)) or an earlier passive-loss carryover worksheet show an unallowed loss from this partnership, even if this year's K-1 shows nothing in boxes 1–3?'

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse owns the partnership interest. The unallowed loss arose on the spouse's earlier separate return, or on a return the spouse filed before the marriage, or the filer's own name appears on the 2024 Form 8582 only through the spouse's activity.
findings.why_no: "A loss from this partnership held back on an earlier return" and "your 2024 Form 8582" read as the filer's own prior return. The filer answers no because they personally had no carryover.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Word the gate as 'Did you or your spouse have a loss from this partnership that was not allowed on an earlier return (including a separate return filed by either of you) and carried forward?'

findings.who: A partner whose earlier return was prepared by software or a paid preparer that silently limited the passive loss and carried it forward. The filer never saw it described as 'held back'. They know it only as a 'suspended' or 'carryover' amount, or not at all.
findings.why_no: "Held back" is not the term on Form 8582 or in preparer summaries, which use "unallowed", "suspended" or "carryover". The filer recalls deducting the K-1 loss and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask the filer to check a document: 'Look at your 2024 return. Is there a Form 8582 whose Part VII, column (c) (unallowed loss) lists this partnership? Preparers may call this a suspended or carryover passive loss.'

findings.who: A partner whose earlier K-1 loss was limited by basis (section 704(d)) or by the at-risk rules (Form 6198), and also by the passive rules. Alternatively, the loss was limited only by basis or at-risk and not by the passive rules.
findings.why_no: "Held back" does not say which limitation is meant. A filer may answer yes for a basis or at-risk carryover that does not belong in Form 8582 column (c). Or a filer may think their only limit was basis-related and answer no, missing the passive-loss part.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Name the source of the amount: 'unallowed passive loss shown on Form 8582, Part VII, column (c)'. Add help text saying that basis or at-risk carryovers (Form 6198) are asked separately.

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A partner with passive losses from this partnership suspended on the 2024 Form 8582 who sold their entire interest in 2025. The final K-1 shows the sale (for example, box 9a/10 or a sale reported on Form 8949/4797) but nothing in boxes 1, 2 or 3.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed. Boxes 1-3 are blank, so the helper is false and the tool never asks about the held-back loss. The filer gives no answer at all.
findings.line: k1p.prior_b1_if (prior years unallowed loss, box 1 activity)
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Don't condition on boxes 1-3. Ask for every K-1: "Does your (or your spouse's) 2024 Form 8582, Part VII (or any prior-year passive loss worksheet), show an unallowed loss for this partnership, even if this year's K-1 shows no amount in box 1, 2 or 3 or you disposed of your interest?"

findings.who: A partner in a still-held passive partnership with a 2024 suspended loss whose 2025 K-1 shows zero or blank in boxes 1-3. The only amounts are in other boxes, such as box 10 net section 1231 gain, box 4 guaranteed payments or box 11 other income, or it is a break-even year.
findings.why_no: The computed gate "box 1, 2 or 3 shows an amount" is false, so the prior-year loss is never asked. That loss must still enter column (c) and can offset other passive income.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity... Enter the total of column (c) from your 2025 Part V on Part I, line 2c"
findings.fix: Gate the prior-year question on the existence of a prior-year unallowed loss for the activity, not on current-year amounts in boxes 1-3.

findings.who: A couple filing jointly in 2025 whose partnership interest belongs to the spouse. The spouse filed single or MFS in 2024, so the suspended loss is on the spouse's own 2024 Form 8582. Or the couple married in 2025.
findings.why_no: The question says "from your 2024 Form 8582". The filer looks at their own 2024 return, finds no Form 8582 and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV/V, Column (c): "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask: "Did your or your spouse's 2024 Form 8582 (from a joint or separate 2024 return) show an unallowed loss for this partnership?"

findings.who: A partner whose 2024 Form 8582 Part VII lists the partnership by name with an unallowed loss, without reference to K-1 boxes. Or the partner's 2024 loss came through a different K-1 box than this year's activity line.
findings.why_no: The question asks about a "held-back loss from the business (box 1)". The 2024 form shows an "unallowed loss" per activity, not per box. The filer doesn't see "held back" or "box 1" anywhere and answers no, or attributes the loss to another box.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity."
findings.fix: Use the form's own words and ask by activity: "Does Part VII, column (c) ('Unallowed loss') of your 2024 Form 8582 show an amount for this partnership's trade or business activity?" Then classify by box afterward.

findings.who: A partner who used software or a preparer in 2024 that carried the suspended loss on a worksheet. The partner has only a summary or doesn't have the 2024 Form 8582 at hand.
findings.why_no: The question names only "your 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c)". A filer who can't find that specific form answers no, although the unallowed loss exists.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity."
findings.fix: Add help text: "Losses from this partnership that were not allowed in earlier years because of the passive activity rules. They usually appear on your 2024 Form 8582 or your preparer's carryover worksheet."

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership sold its rental building in 2025. The final 2025 K-1 reports the sale in box 9a/9c/10 or Form 4797 detail, and boxes 1, 2 and 3 are blank. The partner's 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c), carries a suspended rental real estate loss for this activity.
findings.why_no: The parent gate is computed from this year's K-1 alone ("box 1, 2 or 3 shows an amount"). With all three boxes blank, it is false, so the held-back question is never asked, even though a carryover from an earlier year exists.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Do not gate prior-year unallowed losses on current-year box 1–3 amounts. Ask for every K-1, including a final one: "Did your 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII, column (c)) or carryover worksheet show an unallowed loss for this partnership's rental real estate activity, even if box 2 is blank this year or this is a final K-1?"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership's rental real estate broke even, or whose 2025 box 2 is blank because the activity was idle. The partner still has losses suspended from 2022–2024 on the 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: The computed parent condition is false because box 2 shows no amount this year. The suspended loss carries forward regardless of current-year activity, and current-year income from another passive activity could release it.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Columns (d) and (e): "Combine income and losses in columns (a) through (c) for each activity"; column (c) prior-year unallowed losses are entered for each activity.
findings.fix: Ask about carryovers whenever the filer had this partnership in any prior year (or simply always). The condition should be the existence of a 2024 Part VII column (c) amount, not a current box amount.

findings.who: Spouses filing jointly in 2025 where the K-1 belongs to the spouse, or where the couple filed separately (or the spouse filed single before marriage) in 2024. The suspended loss sits on the spouse's own 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: The filer reads "was a loss held back" or "your 2024 Form 8582" as their own return and sees nothing on it.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Say "you or your spouse" and "any 2024 Form 8582 filed by you or your spouse (joint or separate)".

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 software suspended the loss in its carryover worksheet, or who never attached a Form 8582 in 2024 although a loss was limited. The filer sees no "held back" amount on anything they recognize.
findings.why_no: "Held-back loss" is a classification the filer cannot check, and the cited source (Part VII, column (c) of a 2024 Form 8582) may not be in their records. They answer no instead of reconstructing the amount.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity."
findings.fix: Ask a checkable fact first: "In any earlier year, did this partnership report a rental real estate loss (box 2) that was not fully deducted on your return?" Then direct the filer to the 2024 Form 8582 Part VII, the software carryover report, or a recomputation.

findings.who: A filer whose box 2 loss was suspended in 2021 and never released. The amount carried through every later Form 8582.
findings.why_no: "A loss was held back", asked on the 2025 K-1, reads as a limitation on this year's box 2 loss. The filer thinks of the old loss as an earlier year's matter, not one held back "from it".
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV: "Don't enter a prior-year unallowed loss in column (c) of Part IV unless you actively participated in the activity in both the year the loss arose and the current tax year."
findings.fix: Word it as "from any earlier year, still not deducted as of the end of 2024", not "held back".

findings.who: A partner who did not actively participate, or who lived with their spouse and filed separately, so their box 2 loss was suspended in Part V of the 2024 Form 8582 rather than Part IV.
findings.why_no: The cited help text is from Part IV (active participation). The filer reads the question as covering only the Part IV special-allowance case and answers no for a Part V carryover.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: State that the question covers the box 2 rental real estate carryover whether it was figured in Part IV or Part V, and cite both columns (c).

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A partner in a partnership that rents equipment or other non-real-estate property. Their 2024 box 3 loss was disallowed and appears in 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c). Their 2025 K-1 shows nothing in boxes 1, 2 or 3: the activity broke even, or the only 2025 amounts are elsewhere, such as box 9/10 section 1231 gain or box 19 distributions.
findings.why_no: The parent helper 'Asked only when box 1, 2 or 3 shows an amount' is truthfully false. So the gate is false and the held-back loss question is never asked, even though the activity still carries a prior-year unallowed loss.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Do not make the prior-year question depend on current boxes 1-3. Ask for every Form 1065 K-1, including a final K-1: 'Did your 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII, column (c)) show an unallowed loss for this partnership's activity, whether or not this year's K-1 shows an amount in boxes 1-3?'

findings.who: A partner who disposed of their entire interest during 2025 in a fully taxable transaction. The final K-1 reports the sale or only a box 9/10/11 gain or loss, with boxes 1-3 blank. They have suspended box 3 losses from earlier years.
findings.why_no: Boxes 1, 2 and 3 are empty, so the computed gate is false. The suspended loss, which the disposition frees in full, is treated as zero.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Ask the prior-year unallowed loss question whenever the filer had a 2024 Form 8582 entry for the activity. Also ask it when the K-1 is marked final or the filer reports a disposition, regardless of boxes 1-3.

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 return carried a box 3 rental loss forward on Form 8582. They know it as a 'suspended', 'carryover' or 'unallowed passive' loss.
findings.why_no: The help text 'Held-back loss from other rentals' does not use the IRS words 'prior-year unallowed loss'. A filer may also read 'held back' as something the partnership withheld or did not distribute, not a loss limited on their own 2024 Form 8582.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity.'
findings.fix: Word it as: 'Does your 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c), show a prior-year unallowed (suspended passive) loss for this partnership's other rental activity (box 3)?'

findings.who: A couple filing jointly for 2025 who filed separately, or were unmarried, in 2024. The K-1 belongs to the spouse, whose unallowed box 3 loss is on the spouse's own 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: 'Your 2024 Form 8582' is read by the filer completing the interview as their own 2024 return, which had no Form 8582 or no entry for this activity.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Say 'your or your spouse's 2024 Form 8582 (including a separate 2024 return of the K-1 owner)'.

findings.who: A partner whose activity reported a loss in box 3 in 2024 but reports in box 1 or 2 in 2025, for example after a change in rental classification. The prior-year unallowed loss belongs to the activity, not to the box.
findings.why_no: The question is tied to '(box 3)'. Because this year's box 3 is empty, the filer answers no to the box 3 held-back loss even though the activity's prior-year unallowed loss carries forward.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity.'
findings.fix: Ask per activity: 'Any prior-year unallowed loss for this activity, whatever box it was reported in.' Then route it by the activity's current classification.

findings.who: Any filer reviewing the help text who reads the citation.
findings.why_no: The citation quotes Part IV, which covers rental real estate with active participation. Box 3 other rental activities belong in Part V. A filer who has no actively participated real estate may conclude that the question does not apply to them.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V: 'Use Part V ... for: ... Rental activities other than rental real estate activities.'
findings.fix: Cite i8582 p. 10, Part V, Column (c), instead of Part IV.

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A partner in a fiscal-year partnership (for example, a tax year running February 2024 through January 2025). The K-1 is reported on the 2025 return, and the partner worked 600 hours in the business between February and December 2024.
findings.why_no: Both the gate ("Worked in the business in 2025") and the gated question ("add up to more than 500 hours in 2025") use calendar 2025. Little or none of this partner's work fell in 2025, so they truthfully answer no.
findings.irs_text: "All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the partnership's tax year." (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9)
findings.fix: Ask about "the partnership's tax year shown at the top of this Schedule K-1 (which may begin in 2024)" instead of "in 2025", in both the gate and the hours question.

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 has an empty box 1 but shows trade or business amounts elsewhere: section 179 in box 12, a net section 1231 gain or loss in box 10, other deductions in box 13, or credits. Another case is a real estate professional whose K-1 shows only box 2 rental real estate income or loss. Either partner may work more than 500 hours in the activity.
findings.why_no: The computed gate is false whenever box 1 is blank, so the work and hours questions are never asked. Material participation still decides whether these other amounts are passive.
findings.irs_text: "You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership, and (b) if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity"; "Income (loss), deductions, and credits from an activity are nonpassive if you determine that ... You materially participated" (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9)
findings.fix: Open the gate when the K-1 reports any trade or business item (boxes 1, 4, 9-13, 15, 20 tied to an activity), or any box 2 amount for a filer who is a real estate professional. Do not key it on box 1 alone.

findings.who: A married partner filing separately whose spouse, who is not a partner, works 400 hours in the partnership's business while the partner works 200.
findings.why_no: The help says "on a joint return, your spouse's hours". A filer on a separate return reads this as excluding the spouse's hours, counts 200, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: "Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation." (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9). The text sets no joint-return condition.
findings.fix: Help text: "Count your own hours and your spouse's hours together, whether or not you file a joint return and whether or not your spouse is a partner."

findings.who: On a joint return, a partner who did no work in the business, while their spouse worked full time in it without owning any interest.
findings.why_no: The gate helper reads "Worked in the business in 2025" and does not say "you or your spouse". The partner answers for themselves, says no, and the hours question, whose help does mention the spouse, is never reached.
findings.irs_text: "any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership" (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9)
findings.fix: Ask "Did you or your spouse do any work in this partnership's business during its tax year? (Your spouse's work counts even if your spouse is not a partner.)"

findings.who: A general partner who runs day-to-day operations by making managerial decisions, supervising staff, and negotiating with vendors and customers, but does no hands-on labor.
findings.why_no: The words "worked in the business" suggest hands-on or employee-type labor. The filer thinks of themselves as an owner, not a worker, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: "any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity"; investor work is excluded only if "you aren't directly involved in the day-to-day operations of the activity" (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9)
findings.fix: Ask about "any time spent on the business's operations, including managing, supervising, or making operating decisions, but not only reviewing financial reports as an investor".

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with several activities, with a box 23 statement attached, who works more than 500 hours in one trade or business activity listed on the statement but not in the one whose income is in box 1.
findings.why_no: The gate and the question ask about "the business" as a single unit tied to box 1. The filer answers about the box 1 activity, says no, and is never asked about the other activities.
findings.irs_text: "it'll attach a statement ... that identifies each activity"; "You must determine if you materially participated (a) in each trade or business activity held through the partnership" (i1065sk1 2025 p. 9)
findings.fix: When box 23 is checked, ask the work and hours questions once for each trade or business activity on the statement.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"
p. 9, Work counted toward material participation, "any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership"
